Read the research ↗

How extent is measured

Drag the divider or use the slider to compare two dates from the same observation series. A verified decrease requires full lake and shoreline coverage, a mapped loss of at least 0.005 km², and a loss of at least 20% of the earlier upper estimate after accounting for threshold sensitivity.

Observation sources

Published drainage studies

Field and satellite research found that Toguz-Bulak shrank from 0.021 to 0.002 km² during its August 2019 outburst. Toguz-Bulak field study ↗

Field monitoring documented seasonal drainage at Korumdu. In August 2017 the lake emptied over 17 days. Korumdu field study ↗

What a smaller water surface can indicate

A large reduction can prompt a closer look for drainage. The two published cases show that water can leave a lake rapidly during an outburst or gradually through an outlet. Determining what happened requires field evidence and the timing and conditions of the acquisitions.
